detection.summary: The OLT has 25 offline ONUs, exceeding the approximately 14 expected at baseline, despite healthy OLT metrics and normal sampled optical trends.

diagnosis.root_cause: EPON0/6 has multiple definite ONU offline responses while other ONUs on the same port remain online, identifying a shared splitter-path failure rather than an OLT-wide failure. The two flagged customers are currently offline; their recent sessions and active CRM records reflect prior service, not current online state.
evidence: The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, including its OID subtree, so this is not an OLT failure.
OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are near healthy baselines.
Live probing maps the held interface to EPON0/6 and shows five ONUs with online:0 and responds:true, while four other ONUs on the same port remain online.
The five offline ONU responses have null optical readings, which correctly indicates no current reading rather than strong optical power.
Two or more definite offline ONUs with surviving peers on the same port meets the splitter-failure discriminator.
Both flagged lineids independently return responds:true, online:0, auth_flag Una uth, and MPCP DEREG.
Customer VLAN 1016 is present as expected, so VLAN provisioning is not the cause.
The sampled optical values for online peers are within normal ranges, and the OLT-wide offline count does not override the direct port-level survivor/offline evidence.
diagnosis.discrepancy_detail: The detection trigger reported 11 offline customers, while the live OLT population reports 25 offline and the held EPON0/6 view directly shows five offline ONUs. Cached zero optical values are consistent with missing readings, not measured power; recent sessions and active CRM status are historical/service records and do not contradict the live online:0 responses.

remediation.reason: Multiple ONUs on EPON0/6 are definitively offline while other ONUs on the same PON remain online, indicating a shared splitter-path failure rather than an OLT, router, VLAN, or individual ONU fault. Field inspection is required.
remediation.instructions: Dispatch a technician to inspect the EPON0/6 fibre route, splitter, connectors, and feeder/drop segments. Test optical levels and continuity, repair or replace the failed splitter or damaged fibre path, then verify that all affected ONUs re-register and recover service.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The issue affects five ONUs sharing a splitter path, so resetting individual ONUs would not address the common failure.
The OLT is reachable and healthy, and surviving ONUs on the same port demonstrate that the PON port is not broadly failed.
Customer VLAN 1016 is present and the symptoms are physical offline states, not provisioning or VLAN 46 issues.
A shared splitter-path failure explains the grouped outages better than simultaneous ONU laser ageing.

escalation.summary: Five ONUs on EPON0/6 are definitively offline while other ONUs on the same PON remain online, indicating a shared splitter or fibre-path failure. The OLT is reachable and healthy, optical levels for online peers are normal, and VLAN provisioning is present. Dispatch a technician to inspect and repair the EPON0/6 splitter, connectors, and fibre route, then verify ONU re-registration and service recovery.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
